title: iPSC Cell Culture – Maintenance and Expansion
author: Jacob Marsh
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.9pwh5pe
materials: To resuspend, thaw aliquot On ice .
Tap dish to aid in dislocation of cells.
Pipet cells 2 times only to preserve clumps.

steps.title: Prepare Matrigel coating solution
steps.instruction: Add 12.5 mL cold DMEM/F12 to a tube, pipette up and down twice, then add 1 mL Matrigel per well of a 6‑well plate; store the diluted Matrigel at 4 °C until use.

steps.title: Coat plates with Matrigel
steps.instruction: Dispense the cold Matrigel solution onto each plate (0.5 mL per well of a 12‑well plate, 1 mL per well of a 6‑well plate, 4 mL per well of a 10 cm² plate) while keeping Matrigel on ice, coat for at least 1 hour but no longer than 24 hours, and ensure the coating has not evaporated before plating cells.

steps.title: Thaw iPSC cryovial
steps.instruction: Remove the iPSC cryovial from liquid nitrogen storage, place it in a 37 °C water bath (or thaw in hands) and remove the vial from the bath just before it is completely thawed.

steps.title: Dilute and spin thawed cells
steps.instruction: Transfer the ~1 mL contents of the cryovial into a 15 mL conical tube that already contains 9 mL DMEM/F12 (tube labeled with line name and passage number), spin at 750 rpm for 3 minutes at room temperature, then resuspend the pellet in 2 mL mTesR1 supplemented with the appropriate Rock Inhibitor (5 µM–10 µM) by pipetting twice.

steps.title: Plate thawed iPSCs
steps.instruction: Transfer the 2 mL cell suspension to one well of a pre‑coated 6‑well plate and incubate overnight at 37 °C in 6 % CO₂.

steps.title: Perform daily media changes
steps.instruction: Aspirate spent media each day (media change may be skipped once per week if double‑feeding and confluence is <70 %), then gently add fresh mTesR1 in volumes appropriate for the well size (0.5 mL per well of a 24‑well plate, 2–4 mL per well of a 6‑well plate, 5–10 mL per well of a 10 cm² plate). Incubate at 37 °C in 6 % CO₂.

steps.title: Remove differentiated cells (optional)
steps.instruction: When differentiated cells appear, under a microscope remove them with a p20 tip (small areas) or p200 tip (larger areas) and discard the material in a biohazard bag. Immediately add fresh mTesR1 using the same volumes as above, then incubate at 37 °C in 6 % CO₂ until cultures reach 60–80 % confluence, changing media daily and repeating the cleaning step as needed.

steps.title: Passage iPSCs
steps.instruction: 1. Gently wash cells with 1× PBS (2–3 mL per well). 2. Add Accutase (Gibco A11105‑01) directly to the cells (0.75–1 mL per well of a 6‑well plate, 0.5 mL per well of a 24‑well plate, 3 mL per 10 cm² dish) and incubate at 37 °C for 3–4 minutes. 3. Add DMEM/F12 (2–4 mL per well of a 6‑well plate, 1 mL per well of a 24‑well plate, 9 mL per 10 cm² dish) and scrape gently (p1000 pipette for 24‑well, cell scraper for 6‑well and 10 cm²) to detach all cells. 4. Collect the cell suspension in a 15 mL or 50 mL conical tube (size chosen by volume). If any cells remain, rinse the dish with an additional 2–5 mL DMEM/F12 and add to the tube. 5. Centrifuge at 750 rpm for 3 minutes at room temperature. 6. Aspirate supernatant, leaving 0.5–1 mL to avoid disturbing the pellet. 7. Resuspend the pellet in mTesR1 (2 mL per well of a 6‑well plate) containing the appropriate Rock Inhibitor concentration for the line (10 µM for new or edited lines, 5 µM if sensitivity unknown, 1 µM for all other lines; omit Rock Inhibitor for lines already weaned). 8. Transfer the suspension to a new pre‑coated plate (maintain at least a 1‑hour coating). For routine maintenance dilute cells 1:3 in mTesR1; for expansion plate the entire suspension. 9. Incubate at 37 °C in 6 % CO₂ until cultures reach 60–80 % confluence, changing mTesR1 daily.

steps.title: Freeze iPSCs for storage
steps.instruction: 1. Harvest cells as described in the passage protocol up to the centrifugation step. 2. After the final spin, aspirate supernatant leaving 0.5–1 mL, then resuspend the pellet in mTesR1 without Rock Inhibitor using a volume that yields 1 mL total per cryovial (add 0.5 mL mTesR1 to the pellet). Pipette the suspension 1–2 times only to preserve clumps. 3. Add an equal volume of cold 2× Freezing Media (20 % DMSO in FBS) and pipette once more. 4. Aliquot 1 mL of the cell‑freezing mixture into each pre‑labeled cryovial (label with cell type, line name, passage number, date, and your name). 5. Place the vials in foam racks and freeze at –80 °C for 48–72 hours. 6. Transfer the frozen vials to liquid nitrogen for long‑term storage.
